feature: An SVG logo comes into a video and stays sharp
summary: An SVG now comes into a video like a PNG, from Import Media, a drop on the Library, the picture or the timeline, and it is drawn fresh at whatever size it is shown or exported, so a logo blown up on a 4K frame keeps hard edges. Art tiles on the Media shelf read like the mock: the name over its kind (Acme Logo / svg).
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a recording (Help > Tutorial Sample works). The files used are Scripts/playtest/fixtures/logo/Acme Logo.svg and Sparkle.svg. Walk: Scripts/playtest/library-svg-logo-walk.json.

try.do: File > Import Media (Shift Command I) and pick Acme Logo.svg.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the Acme Logo tile onto the timeline two seconds in.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag Acme Logo.svg from the Finder straight onto the picture.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Set its W to 1000 and H to 400, then do the same to Acme Logo.png placed under it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Zoom the canvas in on the two dots, or export at 2x, and compare the edges (left SVG, right PNG, four times zoomed).
Drag Sparkle.svg from the Finder onto the timeline.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Save with Command S, close and open the project again; the logo is still sharp blown up.

evaluate: Blown up to fill the frame, does the SVG logo look as crisp as the art did in the file?
Does Acme Logo over svg tell you at a glance which tiles are drawings that stay sharp?
Is a picture from the Finder landing on its own Gfx track (and on the shelf) what you expect when you drop it on the timeline?
Does the whole logo sitting centred in its tile read better than a cropped picture would?
rough: Measured bar: across the orange tile's left edge on a 4K frame the SVG blends over 2 pixels (a native draw of the same art: 0), the same logo kept as a bitmap over 12. The drawing is made a step past the frame and brought down, so a growing logo is redrawn a handful of times rather than every frame; that step is the 2 pixels.
A compressed SVG (.svgz) is not taken: macOS does not draw one. It reads as a file with nothing in it.
An SVG let go on a collage slot lands as its own layer instead of filling the slot, because a slot holds pixels.
Opening an SVG with no document open (Finder > Open With) still does nothing; only bringing one into an open document is covered.
Matches the mock's shelf of 'svg, png, a logo': a PNG tile brought in from a file also reads name over kind now (Acme Logo / png); the picked tile's section still gives a PNG's pixel size.

A PNG or SVG from the Finder dropped on the timeline now lands on a Gfx track and on the Library shelf, the way Premiere takes a file dropped on a sequence; before, a PNG landed in the middle of the picture.
